claim: ATR is crucial for mammalian meiosis
source: The phosphatidylinositol 3′ kinase (PI3K)‐related kinase ATR is crucial for mammalian meiosis.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that is supported by the broader scientific literature and the experimental work presented in the manuscript

claim: ATR promotes meiotic progression by coordinating key events in DNA repair, meiotic sex chromosome inactivation (MSCI), and checkpoint-dependent quality control during meiotic prophase I
source: ATR promotes meiotic progression by coordinating key events in DNA repair, meiotic sex chromosome inactivation (MSCI), and checkpoint-dependent quality control during meiotic prophase I.
evidence: This statement summarizes established roles of ATR in meiosis based on prior research

claim: The ATR-dependent meiotic signaling network remains largely unknown
source: Despite its central roles in meiosis, the ATR-dependent meiotic signaling network remains largely unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field

claim: Quantitative analysis of phosphoproteomes identified over 14,000 phosphorylation sites from testes samples
source: Quantitative analysis of phosphoproteomes obtained after germ cell-specific genetic ablation of the ATR activating 9-1-1 complex or treatment with ATR inhibitor identified over 14,000 phosphorylation sites from testes samples, of which 401 phosphorylation sites were found to be dependent on both the 9-1-1 complex and ATR.
evidence: This is a direct result from the phosphoproteomic experiments described in the manuscript

claim: 401 phosphorylation sites were found to be dependent on both the 9-1-1 complex and ATR
source: Quantitative analysis of phosphoproteomes obtained after germ cell-specific genetic ablation of the ATR activating 9-1-1 complex or treatment with ATR inhibitor identified over 14,000 phosphorylation sites from testes samples, of which 401 phosphorylation sites were found to be dependent on both the 9-1-1 complex and ATR.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the phosphoproteomic analysis

claim: ATR-dependent phosphorylation events were identified in crucial DNA damage signaling and DNA repair proteins including TOPBP1, SMC3, MDC1, RAD50, and SLX4
source: Our analyses identified ATR-dependent phosphorylation events in crucial DNA damage signaling and DNA repair proteins including TOPBP1, SMC3, MDC1, RAD50, and SLX4.
evidence: This is a finding from the phosphoproteomic analysis

claim: ATR and RAD1-dependent phosphorylation events were identified in proteins involved in mRNA regulatory processes, including SETX and RANBP3
source: Importantly, we identified ATR and RAD1-dependent phosphorylation events in proteins involved in mRNA regulatory processes, including SETX and RANBP3, whose localization to the sex body was lost upon ATR inhibition.
evidence: This is a finding from the phosphoproteomic analysis combined with immunofluorescence data

claim: The localization of SETX and RANBP3 to the sex body was lost upon ATR inhibition
source: Importantly, we identified ATR and RAD1-dependent phosphorylation events in proteins involved in mRNA regulatory processes, including SETX and RANBP3, whose localization to the sex body was lost upon ATR inhibition.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in the manuscript

claim: An S/T-P-X-K motif was enriched in the set of ATR-dependent events
source: In addition to identifying the expected ATR-targeted S/T-Q motif, we identified enrichment of an S/T-P-X-K motif in the set of ATR-dependent events, suggesting that ATR promotes signaling via proline-directed kinase(s) during meiosis.
evidence: This is a finding from motif analysis of the phosphoproteomic data

claim: ATR promotes signaling via proline-directed kinase(s) during meiosis
source: In addition to identifying the expected ATR-targeted S/T-Q motif, we identified enrichment of an S/T-P-X-K motif in the set of ATR-dependent events, suggesting that ATR promotes signaling via proline-directed kinase(s) during meiosis.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the enrichment of the S/T-P-X-K motif

claim: ATR signaling is important for the proper localization of CDK2 in spermatocytes
source: Indeed, we found that ATR signaling is important for the proper localization of CDK2 in spermatocytes.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data showing altered CDK2 localization upon ATR inhibition

claim: Meiosis is a specialized cellular process whereby a single round of DNA replication is followed by two successive rounds of cell division to produce haploid gametes
source: Meiosis is a specialized cellular process whereby a single round of DNA replication is followed by two successive rounds of cell division to produce haploid gametes.
evidence: This is a well-established definition of meiosis

claim: Meiotic cells must undergo programmed double-strand break (DSB) formation, recombination, and chromosome synapsis to ensure proper chromosome segregation at the first meiotic division
source: To ensure proper chromosome segregation at the first meiotic division, meiotic cells must undergo a series of highly regulated processes, including programmed double-strand break (DSB) formation, recombination, and chromosome synapsis (Keeney et al., 1997; Baudat et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: ATR has well-characterized roles in maintaining genome stability in mitotic cells
source: The serine/threonine-protein kinase ATR (ataxia telangiectasia and Rad-3 related protein) has well-characterized roles in maintaining genome stability in mitotic cells (Yazinski and Zou, 2016; Saldivar et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: ATR plays an essential role in spermatogenesis by promoting meiotic sex chromosome inactivation (MSCI)
source: In mammals, ATR also plays an essential role in spermatogenesis by promoting meiotic sex chromosome inactivation (MSCI), a process that is required for silencing of the X and Y chromosomes (Royo et al., 2010; Pacheco et al., 2018; Widger et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: MSCI is required for silencing of the X and Y chromosomes
source: In mammals, ATR also plays an essential role in spermatogenesis by promoting meiotic sex chromosome inactivation (MSCI), a process that is required for silencing of the X and Y chromosomes (Royo et al., 2010; Pacheco et al., 2018; Widger et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: Impairment of ATR activity results in insufficient MSCI and germ cell elimination at the mid-pachytene stage of prophase I
source: Impairment of ATR activity results in insufficient MSCI and germ cell elimination at the mid-pachytene stage of prophase I (Widger et al., 2018; Royo et al., 2013; Turner, 2007; Menolfi et al., 2018; Fedoriw et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: A major readout of ATR activity during MSCI is the phosphorylation of the histone variant H2AX within the sex body
source: A major readout of ATR activity during MSCI is the phosphorylation of the histone variant H2AX within the dense heterochromatin domain of the nucleus that houses the X and Y chromosomes known as the sex body.
evidence: This is a well-established marker of ATR activity in meiosis

claim: ATR regulates the sex body localization of several DNA damage response proteins such as MDC1 and BRCA1
source: Additionally, ATR regulates the sex body localization of several other DNA damage response proteins such as MDC1 and BRCA1, ultimately resulting in MSCI (Royo et al., 2013; Turner et al., 2004; Ichijima et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: Loss of ATR protein in spermatocytes results in defects in DSB repair and chromosome synapsis
source: Loss of ATR protein in spermatocytes results in defects in DSB repair and chromosome synapsis, implying that ATR regulates several aspects of meiotic progression (Menolfi et al., 2018; Fedoriw et al., 2015; Widger et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: ATR is recruited to RPA-coated ssDNA via interaction with ATRIP in mitotic cells
source: ATR is recruited to RPA-coated ssDNA via interaction with ATRIP (ATR interacting protein) (Zou and Elledge, 2003), while the 9A-1-1 (RAD9A-RAD1-HUS1) checkpoint clamp is independently loaded at the dsDNA-ssDNA junction by the RAD17-RFC clamp loader (Delacroix et al., 2007; Eichinger and Jentsch, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research on ATR activation in mitotic cells

claim: The 9-1-1 checkpoint clamp is loaded at the dsDNA-ssDNA junction by the RAD17-RFC clamp loader
source: ATR is recruited to RPA-coated ssDNA via interaction with ATRIP (ATR interacting protein) (Zou and Elledge, 2003), while the 9A-1-1 (RAD9A-RAD1-HUS1) checkpoint clamp is independently loaded at the dsDNA-ssDNA junction by the RAD17-RFC clamp loader (Delacroix et al., 2007; Eichinger and Jentsch, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: TOPBP1 interacts with the c-terminal tail of RAD9A and directly activates ATR via its ATR activation domain (AAD)
source: The ATR activating protein, TOPBP1 (topoisomerase binding protein 1), then interacts with the c-terminal tail of RAD9A and directly activates ATR via its ATR activation domain (AAD) (Burtelow et al., 2001; Takeishi et al., 2015; Roos-Mattjus et al., 2003; Thada and Cortez, 2019; Kumagai et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: Conditional depletion of TOPBP1 in germ cells results in defective MSCI as well as loss of ATR and H2AX phosphorylation in the sex body
source: Conditional depletion of TOPBP1 in germ cells results in defective MSCI as well as loss of ATR and H2AX phosphorylation in the sex body (ElInati et al., 2017; Perera et al., 2004; Jeon et al., 2019 ).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: TOPBP1 plays a prominent role in mediating the strong ATR signaling observed during pachynema
source: The results suggest a prominent role for TOPBP1 in mediating the strong ATR signaling observed during pachynema.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited studies showing TOPBP1's role in ATR activation during meiosis

claim: ETAA1 can directly activate ATR at RPA-coated ssDNA at replication forks
source: ETAA1 can directly activate ATR at RPA-coated ssDNA at replication forks and is thought to be important for ATR activation during unchallenged DNA replication and unlikely to function in meiosis (ElInati et al., 2017; Bass and Cortez, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: ETAA1 is unlikely to function in meiosis
source: ETAA1 can directly activate ATR at RPA-coated ssDNA at replication forks and is thought to be important for ATR activation during unchallenged DNA replication and unlikely to function in meiosis (ElInati et al., 2017; Bass and Cortez, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: ATR preferentially phosphorylates proteins at S/T-Q motifs
source: Once activated, ATR preferentially phosphorylates proteins at S/T-Q motifs (Kim et al., 1999; O'Neill et al., 2000; Bastos de Oliveira et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: In mitotic cells, ATR-mediated phosphorylation of H2AX and MDC1 contributes to checkpoint activation by enhancing ATR phosphorylation of CHK1/CHK2, resulting in checkpoint-mediated cell cycle arrest
source: In mitotic cells, ATR-mediated phosphorylation of the histone variant H2AX (hereafter referred to as γH2AX) and the scaffold protein MDC1 contributes to checkpoint activation by enhancing ATR phosphorylation of the downstream kinases CHK1/CHK2, resulting in checkpoint-mediated cell cycle arrest (Brown and Baltimore, 2003; Lou et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: In meiosis, ATR phosphorylates H2AX and MDC1
source: In meiosis, ATR also phosphorylates H2AX and MDC1, but, intriguingly, this strong induction of ATR activity observed during normal spermatogenesis is compatible with the progression of the meiotic cell cycle (Kolas et al., 2005; Fernandez-Capetillo et al., 2003; Ichijima et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: Strong induction of ATR activity observed during normal spermatogenesis is compatible with the progression of the meiotic cell cycle
source: In meiosis, ATR also phosphorylates H2AX and MDC1, but, intriguingly, this strong induction of ATR activity observed during normal spermatogenesis is compatible with the progression of the meiotic cell cycle (Kolas et al., 2005; Fernandez-Capetillo et al., 2003; Ichijima et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: Hundreds of ATR targets have been characterized using quantitative phosphoproteomics in mitotic cells
source: While hundreds of ATR targets have been characterized using quantitative phosphoproteomics mitotic cells (Bass and Cortez, 2019; Lanz et al., 2019; Wagner et al., 2016), much less is understood about ATR signaling in meiosis.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: Much less is understood about ATR signaling in meiosis compared to mitotic cells
source: While hundreds of ATR targets have been characterized using quantitative phosphoproteomics mitotic cells (Bass and Cortez, 2019; Lanz et al., 2019; Wagner et al., 2016), much less is understood about ATR signaling in meiosis.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field

claim: ATR depletion results in embryonic lethality
source: Given that ATR depletion results in embryonic lethality (Brown and Baltimore, 2003; Brown and Baltimore, 2000; de Klein et al., 2000), we used a genetic model of impairing ATR signaling whereby the 9-1-1 component RAD1 is conditionally depleted under the germ cell-specific Stra8-Cre.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: Depletion of RAD1 in germ cells is anticipated to disrupt all potential 9-1-1 complexes and significantly impair ATR signaling
source: Depletion of RAD1 in germ cells is anticipated to disrupt all potential 9-1-1 complexes, including those that could form with the testes-specific paralogs Hus1b and Rad9b , and therefore significantly impair ATR signaling (Pereira et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a prediction based on the role of RAD1 in the 9-1-1 complex and supported by a citation

claim: 4 hr of ATRi treatment was enough to cause a robust reduction in sex body γH2AX localization in pachynema staged cells
source: We observed that 4 hr of ATRi treatment was enough to cause a robust reduction in sex body γH2AX localization in pachynema staged cells (Figure 1C and D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in the figures

claim: A total of 49,843 phosphorylation sites were identified between the eight experiments
source: HILIC pre-fractionation of TMT-labeled phosphopeptides allowed in-depth quantitative phosphoproteomic analysis, resulting in a total of 49,843 phosphorylation sites identified between the eight experiments (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the mass spectrometry analysis

claim: The final list yielded 14,956 quantitated phosphorylation sites after filtering
source: After selecting for high-quality phosphosites (localization score >0.85) and considering only phosphopeptides identified in both the AZ20 and RAD1 cKO datasets in at least two independent replicates, our final list yielded 14,956 quantitated phosphorylation sites (Figure 1E and F, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result after data filtering

claim: Approximately twofold more differentially phosphorylated peptides were found in Q2 compared to each of the other quadrants
source: By comparing the number of phosphopeptides present in each of the four quadrants (Q1–Q4), we observed a biased distribution with approximately twofold more differentially phosphorylated peptides in Q2 compared to each of the other quadrants, consistent with a model that the primary mode of ATR activation during meiosis is RAD1-dependent (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the phosphoproteomic data analysis

claim: The primary mode of ATR activation during meiosis is RAD1-dependent
source: By comparing the number of phosphopeptides present in each of the four quadrants (Q1–Q4), we observed a biased distribution with approximately twofold more differentially phosphorylated peptides in Q2 compared to each of the other quadrants, consistent with a model that the primary mode of ATR activation during meiosis is RAD1-dependent (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an inference based on the biased distribution of phosphopeptides in Q2

claim: Q2 is enriched for gene ontology categories such as nucleic acid metabolism, chromosome organization, and cell cycle
source: Gene enrichment analysis of each filtered quadrant revealed that Q2 is enriched for gene ontology categories such as nucleic acid metabolism, chromosome organization, and cell cycle (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, Supplementary file 2), consistent with the expected roles for ATR and RAD1 in these processes.
evidence: This is a result from gene ontology analysis of the phosphoproteomic data

claim: 29 MDC1 phosphorylation sites were detected, including 8 sites in Q2 (ATR- and RAD1-dependent) and 21 sites that were not dependent on ATR phosphorylation
source: We detected 29 MDC1 phosphorylation sites, including 8 sites in Q2 (ATR- and RAD1-dependent) and 21 sites that were not dependent on ATR phosphorylation (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the phosphoproteomic analysis of MDC1

claim: Phosphorylation of MDC1 at threonine 4 showed a significant loss of signal at the sex body upon 4 hr of ATRi treatment
source: We also probed the phosphorylation of MDC1 at threonine 4 using a phospho-specific antibody on meiotic spreads and observed a significant loss of signal at the sex body upon 4 hr of ATRi treatment (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 4B and C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data

claim: The set of Q2 sites with an S/T-Q motif was enriched in proteins involved in DNA repair, including MDC1, UIMC1 (RAP80), and the components of the MRN complex RAD50 and NBN (NBS1)
source: Notably, the set of Q2 sites with an S/T-Q motif was enriched in proteins involved in DNA repair, including MDC1, UIMC1 (RAP80), and the components of the MRN complex RAD50 and NBN (NBS1) (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is a result from analysis of S/T-Q motif-containing phosphorylation sites in Q2

claim: The group of S/T-Q sites in Q2 included proteins involved in RNA metabolism and chromatin regulation
source: The group of S/T-Q sites in Q2 also included proteins involved in RNA metabolism and chromatin regulation (Figure 3D and E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is a result from analysis of S/T-Q motif-containing phosphorylation sites in Q2

claim: S/T-Q sites in proteins involved in RNA metabolism (SETX, XPO5, and RANBP3) displayed high ATR dependency
source: Notably, S/T-Q sites in proteins involved in RNA metabolism (SETX, XPO5, and RANBP3) displayed high ATR dependency (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D) and were detected in both the 4 hr and 2.5–3-day ATRi datasets (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a result from the phosphoproteomic analysis

claim: Serine 353 in Senataxin (SETX) was downregulated upon RAD1 loss and ATR inhibition
source: We found serine 353 in Senataxin (SETX), an RNA:DNA helicase with established roles in transcriptional regulation and genome maintenance (Cohen et al., 2018; Groh et al., 2017) to be downregulated upon RAD1 loss and ATR inhibition (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a result from the phosphoproteomic analysis

claim: Senataxin disruption is associated with male infertility in humans
source: Senataxin disruption is associated with male infertility in humans, and Setx-/- male mice are infertile resulting from arrest at the pachytene stage in meiosis I (Becherel et al., 2019; Becherel et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: Setx-/- male mice are infertile resulting from arrest at the pachytene stage in meiosis I
source: Senataxin disruption is associated with male infertility in humans, and Setx-/- male mice are infertile resulting from arrest at the pachytene stage in meiosis I (Becherel et al., 2019; Becherel et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: Senataxin localizes to the XY chromosomes and promotes the localization of ATR, γH2AX, and other DNA repair and checkpoint factors to the sex body during MSCI
source: Senataxin localizes to the XY chromosomes and promotes the localization of ATR, γH2AX, and other DNA repair and checkpoint factors to the sex body during MSCI (Yeo et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research

claim: Senataxin accumulation at the sex body was significantly reduced in pachytene spreads derived from ATRi-treated mice
source: Strikingly, Senataxin accumulation at the sex body was significantly reduced in pachytene spreads derived from ATRi-treated mice (Figure 4A and B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data

claim: No enrichment of Senataxin was observed around any selection of chromosomes in pachytene-like spreads from Rad1 cKO mice
source: While it is difficult to morphologically distinguish the X and Y chromosomes in the Rad1 cKO spreads, we observed no enrichment of Senataxin around any selection of chromosomes in pachytene-like spreads with four or more synapsed autosomes in both 8–12-week and 14-day-old mice (Figure 4C and D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data

claim: ATR promotes the recruitment or retention of Senataxin at the sex body
source: Our results further suggest that ATR promotes the recruitment or retention of Senataxin at the sex body, consistent with a model in which Senataxin and ATR act in a feed-forward loop to cooperatively promote their recruitment and efficient sex body formation and MSCI.
evidence: This is an inference based on the immunofluorescence data showing loss of Senataxin localization upon ATR inhibition

claim: Senataxin and ATR act in a feed-forward loop to cooperatively promote their recruitment and efficient sex body formation and MSCI
source: Our results further suggest that ATR promotes the recruitment or retention of Senataxin at the sex body, consistent with a model in which Senataxin and ATR act in a feed-forward loop to cooperatively promote their recruitment and efficient sex body formation and MSCI.
evidence: This is a speculative model based on the data and prior research

claim: RANBP3 phosphorylation at serine 283 was downregulated upon RAD1 loss and ATR inhibition
source: Another protein with a S/T-Q phosphorylation site downregulated upon RAD1 loss and ATR inhibition was RANBP3 (phosphorylation at serine 283) (Figure 3D and E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a result from the phosphoproteomic analysis

claim: RANBP3 localizes to the sex body at pachynema in cells derived from wild-type or vehicle-treated mice
source: We investigated the localization of RANBP3 in meiotic spreads and found that in cells derived from wild-type or vehicle-treated mice, RANBP3 localizes to the sex body at pachynema (Figure 4E and F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data

claim: The accumulation of RANBP3 is significantly lost at the sex body derived from ATRi-treated mice and at all chromosome cores in Rad1 cKO pachytene-like spreads
source: The accumulation of RANBP3 is significantly lost at the sex body derived from ATRi-treated mice and at all chromosome cores in Rad1 cKO pachytene-like spreads in both 8–12-week and 14-day-old mice (Figure 4G and H, Figure 4—figure supplement 2C and D), suggesting a role for ATR in the recruitment or retention of RANBP3 at the sex body.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data

claim: ATR plays a role in the recruitment or retention of RANBP3 at the sex body
source: The accumulation of RANBP3 is significantly lost at the sex body derived from ATRi-treated mice and at all chromosome cores in Rad1 cKO pachytene-like spreads in both 8–12-week and 14-day-old mice (Figure 4G and H, Figure 4—figure supplement 2C and D), suggesting a role for ATR in the recruitment or retention of RANBP3 at the sex body.
evidence: This is an inference based on the immunofluorescence data

claim: Most phosphorylation sites in Q2 are not in the S/T-Q motif
source: Despite phosphorylation at the S/T-Q motif being enriched in Q2, it still represented only a small portion of the RAD1- and ATR-dependent sites identified in both datasets for 4 hr and 2.5–3 days of ATRi (Figure 5A, Supplementary files 1 and 3).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the phosphoproteomic data

claim: ATR is able to phosphorylate other motifs and/or directly or indirectly regulate the activity of other kinases or phosphatases during meiosis
source: The finding that most phosphorylation sites in Q2 are not in the S/T-Q motif suggests that ATR is able to phosphorylate other motifs and/or directly or indirectly regulate the activity of other kinases or phosphatases during meiosis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that most Q2 sites are not S/T-Q

claim: A large fraction of phosphorylation sites in Q2 contain a proline at the +1 position
source: First, analysis of the amino acid at the +1 position following the phosphorylated S/T residue revealed that a large fraction of phosphorylation sites contain a proline at the +1 position (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a result from motif analysis of the phosphoproteomic data

claim: The proportion of S/T-P sites in Q2 increased from ~42% in the 4 hr ATRi dataset to over 65% in the 2.5–3-day ATRi dataset
source: Interestingly, the proportion of S/T-P sites in Q2 increased from ~42% in the 4 hr ATRi dataset to over 65% in the 2.5–3-day ATRi dataset, suggesting that these sites could represent the impairment of downstream signaling events mediated indirectly by a kinase or phosphatase regulated by ATR, and would therefore take longer to be impaired after ATR inhibition.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the phosphoproteomic data

claim: S/T-P sites in Q2 could represent the impairment of downstream signaling events mediated indirectly by a kinase or phosphatase regulated by ATR
source: Interestingly, the proportion of S/T-P sites in Q2 increased from ~42% in the 4 hr ATRi dataset to over 65% in the 2.5–3-day ATRi dataset, suggesting that these sites could represent the impairment of downstream signaling events mediated indirectly by a kinase or phosphatase regulated by ATR, and would therefore take longer to be impaired after ATR inhibition.
evidence: This is an inference based on the temporal dynamics of S/T-P site depletion

claim: The matrices for both the 4 hr and 2.5–3-day ATRi treatment datasets revealed enrichment for K at +3 position in the set of ATR and RAD1-dependent sites
source: The matrices for both the 4 hr and 2.5–3-day ATRi treatment datasets revealed enrichment for K at +3 position in the set of ATR and RAD1-dependent sites.
evidence: This is a result from motif analysis of the phosphoproteomic data

claim: Most ATR and RAD1-dependent phosphosites with K at +3 contain a P at the +1 position
source: Close inspection of the group of ATR and RAD1-dependent phosphosites with K at +3 revealed that most contain a P at the +1 position, both for the 4 hr and 2.5–3-day ATRi datasets (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), suggesting the enrichment of an S/T-P-X-K motif.
evidence: This is a result from motif analysis of the phosphoproteomic data

claim: There is enrichment of an S/T-P-X-K motif in ATR and RAD1-dependent phosphosites
source: Close inspection of the group of ATR and RAD1-dependent phosphosites with K at +3 revealed that most contain a P at the +1 position, both for the 4 hr and 2.5–3-day ATRi datasets (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), suggesting the enrichment of an S/T-P-X-K motif.
evidence: This is an inference based on the motif analysis

claim: Comparison of the prevalence of S/T-P-X-K motifs in Q2 to the set of unregulated phosphosites revealed substantial enrichments of the S/T-P-X-K motif in both the 4 hr and 2.5–3-day ATRi Q2 datasets
source: Indeed, comparison of the prevalence of S/T-P-X-K motifs in Q2 (ATR- and RAD1-dependent) to the set of unregulated phosphosites found in the center of the dataset revealed substantial enrichments of the S/T-P-X-K motif in both the 4 hr and 2.5–3-day ATRi Q2 datasets (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a result from motif analysis comparing Q2 to center sites

claim: The enrichment of S/T-P-X-K motif was greater in the 2.5–3-day ATRi dataset, reaching over 15% of all Q2 sites, as compared to comprising only 3% in the center (unregulated) sites
source: The enrichment was greater in the 2.5–3-day ATRi dataset, reaching over 15% of all Q2 sites, as compared to comprising only 3% in the center (unregulated) sites.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from motif analysis

claim: ATR is regulating the activity of one or more kinases that have a preference for S/T-P-X-K motif
source: These results suggest that ATR is regulating the activity of one or more kinases that have a preference for S/T-P-X-K motif.
evidence: This is an inference based on the enrichment of the S/T-P-X-K motif in ATR-dependent sites

claim: The S/T-P-X-K motif fits the canonical preferential motif for the master cell cycle kinases CDK1 and CDK2
source: Notably, this motif fits the canonical preferential motif for the master cell cycle kinases CDK1 and CDK2.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of CDK1 and CDK2 substrate specificity

claim: CDK2 localizes to the core as well as to the ends of chromosomes
source: We observed that CDK2 localizes to the core as well as to the ends of chromosomes, similar to previously reported (Tu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data and a citation to prior research

claim: Autosomal localization of CDK2 is significantly disrupted by ATRi, and this effect could be observed already at 4hr after ATRi treatment
source: Image analysis revealed that autosomal localization of CDK2 is significantly disrupted by ATRi, and surprisingly, this effect could be observed already at 4hr after ATRi treatment (Figure 5C and D, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data

claim: 4 hr of ATRi treatment does not result in major changes in cellular composition
source: Importantly, 4 hr of ATRi treatment does not result in major changes in cellular composition (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A and B), supporting that the changes in S/T-P-X-K sites observed at 4 hr after ATRi are likely due to specific alterations in an ATR signaling axis rather than indirect effects due to gross changes in testis cellularity.
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis

claim: Different downstream S/T-P-X-K sites are likely under distinct dynamics of phosphorylation and dephosphorylation following ATRi
source: The identification of more Q2 S/T-P-X-K sites in the 2.5–3-day ATRi dataset when compared to the 4 hr ATRi dataset suggests that different downstream S/T-P-X-K are likely under distinct dynamics of phosphorylation and dephosphorylation following ATRi.
evidence: This is an inference based on the temporal dynamics of S/T-P-X-K site detection

claim: CDK2 is critical for meiotic prophase I progression
source: CDK2 has established roles in cell cycle regulation and, in the context of meiosis, is critical for meiotic prophase I progression (Berthet et al., 2003; Ortega et al., 2003; Chauhan et al., 2016; Palmer et al., 2020; Singh et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research

claim: Gene ontology analysis of proteins with S/T-P-X-K motif phosphorylation in quadrant 2 revealed a significant enrichment for genes involved in regulation of the cell cycle, including CDC20 and RBL1
source: Consistent with the model that CDK2 activity is impaired by ATRi and RAD1 loss of function, gene ontology analysis of proteins with S/T-P-X-K motif phosphorylation in quadrant 2 revealed a significant enrichment for genes involved in regulation of the cell cycle, including CDC20 and RBL1 (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a result from gene ontology analysis

claim: Several proteins involved in the biogenesis of piRNAs were phosphorylated at S/T-P sites in a RAD1- and ATR-dependent manner
source: Interestingly, we noticed that several proteins involved in the biogenesis of piRNAs were phosphorylated at S/T-P sites in a RAD1- and ATR-dependent manner (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a result from the phosphoproteomic analysis

claim: piRNAs play key roles in spermatogenesis by preventing retrotransposon integration during meiosis
